record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update ignores the request body and persists nothing — it re-renders the exact state the fetch_embedding before_filter already loaded — while the frontend saveChanges action sends `embedding.update({})` against it. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 success while saving nothing, so the first client that PUTs real payload data silently loses it; the saveChanges action is additionally dead code since no element in embedding.hbs triggers it.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read `params` or persist anything; it simply re-serializes `@embedding` created by `fetch_embedding` (an `OpenStruct` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). Yet `config/routes.rb` adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`. This PUT endpoint will return success while ignoring any request body, which is misleading/broken behavior (silent no-op), and the `saveChanges` action appears unused by `embedding.hbs` (no button/action wired).

result.rationale: Every factual claim is verifiable in the diff: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` only, reading no params and saving nothing (persistence for hosts goes through EmbeddableHostsController instead); the route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` exists; the frontend `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` (empty payload); and embedding.hbs contains only the addHost button and embeddable-host rows (`deleteHost`), so nothing triggers saveChanges — it is dead code.
